title: A Fact Changes What You Know

scenes.tts: A woman's brother has cystic fibrosis, but her parents do not have it, and neither does she. What is the chance that she carries a cystic fibrosis allele? The tempting answer is one half, but under the standard model it is two thirds. You cannot cross people, so geneticists read pedigrees, the families that already exist. Here is why the answer is two thirds.
scenes.visual: A pedigree: unaffected parents, a filled brother, and the woman with a question mark. Two answer chips, 1/2 and 2/3, appear beside it.
scenes.narration: A woman's brother has cystic fibrosis, but her parents do not have it, and neither does she. What is the chance that she carries a cystic fibrosis allele? The tempting answer is one half, but under the standard model it is two thirds. You cannot cross people, so geneticists read pedigrees, the families that already exist. Here is why the answer is two thirds.

scenes.tts: Start with her parents. Two unaffected parents have an affected child, so both must be carriers. An affected person has two copies of the recessive allele, and a carrier has one copy and usually shows no trait. We write the carrier genotype as capital A, small a. This assumes full penetrance, no new mutations, and correct relationships.
scenes.caption: Start with her parents. Two unaffected parents have an affected child, so both must be carriers. An affected person has two copies of the recessive allele, and a carrier has one copy and usually shows no trait. We write the carrier genotype as Aa. This assumes full penetrance, no new mutations, and correct relationships.
scenes.visual: Same pedigree. Each parent gets a pair of chromosome bars, one with the normal allele A and one with the recessive allele a.
scenes.narration: Start with her parents. Two unaffected parents have an affected child, so both must be carriers. An affected person has two copies of the recessive allele, and a carrier has one copy and usually shows no trait. We write the carrier genotype as Aa. This assumes full penetrance, no new mutations, and correct relationships.

scenes.tts: Now cross the two carriers, with each parent giving one allele. Four outcomes are equally likely: capital A, capital A; capital A, small a, with the A from the mother. Then small a, capital A, with the A from the father; and small a, small a. Each outcome has probability one quarter.
scenes.caption: Now cross the two carriers, with each parent giving one allele. Four outcomes are equally likely: AA; Aa, with the A from the mother. Then aA, with the A from the father; and aa. Each outcome has probability 1/4.
scenes.visual: A two by two square fills with the four genotypes drawn as chromosome pairs, each marked 1/4.
scenes.narration: Now cross the two carriers, with each parent giving one allele. Four outcomes are equally likely: AA; Aa, with the A from the mother. Then aA, with the A from the father; and aa. Each outcome has probability 1/4.

scenes.tts: Now use what you know. Before this fact, all four outcomes were possible, but she is unaffected. So the small a, small a outcome is impossible, and we cross it out. Three equal outcomes remain, and two of them are carriers. That is two out of three.
scenes.caption: Now use what you know. Before this fact, all four outcomes were possible, but she is unaffected. So the aa outcome is impossible, and we cross it out. Three equal outcomes remain, and two of them are carriers. That is two out of three.
scenes.visual: The unaffected woman appears beside the square. The aa cell is crossed out, the two carrier cells light up, and 2 of 3 appears.
scenes.narration: Now use what you know. Before this fact, all four outcomes were possible, but she is unaffected. So the aa outcome is impossible, and we cross it out. Three equal outcomes remain, and two of them are carriers. That is two out of three.

scenes.tts: Check the arithmetic. This is a conditional probability: the chance of one thing, given something you know. Carriers hold one half of the probability, and the three remaining outcomes hold three quarters. One half divided by three quarters is two thirds. The old answer, one half, is the carrier chance before you learn that she is unaffected.
scenes.caption: Check the arithmetic. This is a conditional probability: the chance of one thing, given something you know. Carriers hold 1/2 of the probability, and the three remaining outcomes hold 3/4. 1/2 divided by 3/4 is 2/3. The old answer, 1/2, is the carrier chance before you learn that she is unaffected.
scenes.visual: A bar of four quarter blocks. Brackets mark the carriers (1/2) and the three remaining blocks (3/4); the equation (1/2) / (3/4) = 2/3 is written out.
scenes.narration: Check the arithmetic. This is a conditional probability: the chance of one thing, given something you know. Carriers hold 1/2 of the probability, and the three remaining outcomes hold 3/4. 1/2 divided by 3/4 is 2/3. The old answer, 1/2, is the carrier chance before you learn that she is unaffected.

scenes.tts: Knowing she is unaffected removed one of four outcomes, so the denominator shrank from four to three. It did not change her genotype. It changed what we know about it. Conditioning can use more than one fact, and Bayes rule combines what you believed before with how likely the new evidence is. These numbers are an exercise in the logic, not a risk figure for a real family.
